title: Isolation and Extraction of Plant Nuclei in Plug
author: Karine Labadie
materials: NIB Buffer : 200 ml : freshly prepared Reagent Final concentration 1 Tris ph8 10 mM 2 EDTA 10 mM 3 KCl 80 mM 4 Sucrose 0.5 M 5 PVP 40 2 % 6 Spermine 1 mM 7 Spermidine 1 mM 8 H2O qsp 200 ml Adjust the Ph to 9.4 then filter at 0.22 µm

Screw a sieve caps onto the tube and empty the solution. Change the proteinase K Solution bath as before. Incubate in thermomixer overnight at 50 °C with intermittent mixing Mixing cycle : 10 seconds at 450 rpm followed by 10 minutes at 0 rpm Overnight 50 °C

steps.title: Cool mortar with liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Place the mortar and pestle in liquid nitrogen and wait until bubbling stops, keeping the tools fully chilled.

steps.title: Grind frozen plant tissue
steps.instruction: Add 2 g of frozen plant sample to the chilled mortar and grind without adding more liquid nitrogen until a fine powder is obtained (≈2 min).

steps.title: Prepare NIBTM extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Place a beaker on ice, add a magnetic stir bar, then add 20 mL of NIBTM (10 mL g⁻¹ of leaves) and stir gently.

steps.title: Extract nuclei on ice
steps.instruction: Transfer the powder to the beaker containing NIBTM and shake gently on ice for 10 min.

steps.title: Filter homogenate and recover nuclei
steps.instruction: Filter the mixture sequentially to remove debris and collect nuclei.

substeps.instruction: Filter through autoclaved filters placed on a funnel (2 layers of cheesecloth – Thermo Fisher Catalog #22055053 – and 2 layers of Miracloth – Merck Millipore Catalog #475855). After filtration, squeeze the filters to recover remaining liquid.
Pass the filtrate through a 40 µm cell strainer (Falcon, Corning Catalog #352340) into a new 50 mL tube.

steps.title: First centrifugation of homogenate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 800 × g, 4 °C for 20 min with acceleration and deceleration set to level 3.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in cold NIBTM
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant, gently resuspend the pellet on ice (use a brush if the pellet does not recover), and add 20 mL of cold NIBTM.

steps.title: Low‑speed spin to remove debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge again at 60 × g, 4 °C for 2 min with acceleration/deceleration level 3 to pellet residues and unlysed cells.

steps.title: Filter supernatant through 40 µm sieve
steps.instruction: Pass the resulting supernatant through a 40 µm cell sieve into a fresh 50 mL tube.

steps.title: Pellet nuclei (high‑speed)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the filtered suspension at 800 × g, 4 °C for 15 min with acceleration/deceleration level 3 to pellet the nuclei.

steps.title: Wash nuclei three times with NIBT
steps.instruction: Perform three successive washes of the nuclei pellet with cold NIBT buffer.

substeps.instruction: For each wash: remove supernatant, gently resuspend the pellet, add 40 mL of cold NIBT, then centrifuge at 800 × g, 4 °C for 15 min (acc/dec = 3).

steps.title: Final wash with NIB buffer
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet once with 30 mL of cold NIB buffer and centrifuge at 800 × g, 4 °C for 15 min (acc/dec = 3).

steps.title: Resuspend nuclei for plug preparation
steps.instruction: Resuspend the final pellet in the residual buffer (≈200 µL), transfer to a 1.5 mL tube, and centrifuge at 800 × g, 4 °C for 15 min (acc/dec = 3).

steps.title: Adjust nuclei volume per plug
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant with a pipette and resuspend the nuclei pellet in 60 µL of cell‑suspension buffer per plug; adjust the number of plugs according to pellet size.

steps.title: Prepare 0.8 % low‑melting agarose
steps.instruction: Use UltraPure™ Low‑Melting Point Agarose (Catalog #16520‑100) to obtain a final agarose concentration of 0.8 %.

steps.title: Melt and equilibrate agarose
steps.instruction: Melt the agarose at 70 °C for 5 min, then equilibrate at 43 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Mix nuclei with 2 % agarose
steps.instruction: Pre‑heat the nuclei suspension to 43 °C for 3 min, add the calculated volume of 2 % agarose (see table), and mix gently with a wide‑bore tip to avoid bubbles.

steps.title: Dispense and polymerise plugs
steps.instruction: Immediately dispense 100 µL of the nuclei‑agarose mixture per well using a wide‑bore tip and allow polymerisation on ice for 15 min.

steps.title: Prepare proteinase K digestion solution
steps.instruction: In a 50 mL tube mix 200 µL proteinase K enzyme (20 mg mL⁻¹) with 2.5 mL lysis buffer.

steps.title: Proteinase K digestion of plugs
steps.instruction: Transfer the agarose plugs to the tube containing the proteinase K solution and incubate in a thermomixer for 2 h at 50 °C with intermittent mixing (10 s at 450 rpm followed by 10 min static).

steps.title: Prepare RNase wash solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare TE 10:50 as Wash Buffer and TE 10:5 for RNase treatment.

steps.title: RNase digestion of plugs
steps.instruction: Rinse plugs three times with 10 mL of TE 10:5, then add 2.5 mL TE 10:5 plus 50 µL RNase A (Qiagen Catalog #19101). Incubate 1 h at 37 °C with intermittent mixing.

steps.title: Post‑RNase washes
steps.instruction: Rinse the plugs three times with 10 mL of Wash Buffer (TE 10:50). Plugs may be stored at 4 °C in Wash Buffer at this stage.

steps.title: Agarase treatment – washes
steps.instruction: Wash the plugs four times with 10 mL wash buffer for 15 min each at room temperature with gentle agitation (15 rpm) on a horizontal platform mixer.

steps.title: Agarase treatment – melt and digest
steps.instruction: Transfer each plug to a 1.5 mL tube with a sterile spatula, melt in a 70 °C water bath for 2 min, then place at 43 °C for 5 min. Add 2 µL agarase, mix gently by rotating the tip, and incubate 45 min at 43 °C.

steps.title: Equilibrate dialysis membrane
steps.instruction: Place 10 mL 1× TE buffer in a 6 cm Petri dish, float a 0.1 µm dialysis membrane on the surface, cover the dish and let the membrane equilibrate for 15 min.

steps.title: Dialyse DNA sample
steps.instruction: Deposit the entire plug‑derived sample in the centre of the equilibrated membrane using a wide‑bore tip, cover the dish and dialyse for 45 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Collect and resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Transfer the dialysed DNA to a 1.5 mL micro‑fuge tube with a wide‑bore tip, allow the DNA to resuspend overnight at room temperature, then store for 2 days at 4 °C before quality control.

steps.title: Sample quality control
steps.instruction: Sonicate an aliquot of DNA for 10 min, quantify the sample with a Qubit HS assay, and visualise 1 µL on a TapeStation, pulsed‑field gel, or Femto Pulse to assess molecular‑weight distribution.

steps.title: Optional microscopic observation
steps.instruction: Take a 100 µL aliquot of the nuclei suspension, stain with DAPI, and examine under a fluorescence microscope to confirm the presence of nuclei.
